messages:
Maya: Quick note  closing week forecast shows a potential review surge for Backend and Platform teams (project deadlines + review close). We need a mitigation plan.

Owen: What's the projected spike? Numbers?

Maya: Estimated additional 420 handbacks across two days. Peak expected between 09:00-15:00 PT on final day.

Sasha: Oof. Can we throttle new assignments or prioritize items by age/impact?

ops-bot: Current options: (1) auto-throttle new assignments to reviewers >24 pending, (2) prioritize by "feedback_age" then "impact_score", (3) temporarily expand volunteer pool with auto-assign.

Priya: I'm worried about calibration integrity if we change assignment ordering.

Maya: Agreed. Proposal: for surge window, keep calibration sample frozen, but route non-calibration items to volunteer pool and enable temporary auto-assign for volunteers only. That preserves calibration buckets.

Owen: Who can be volunteers? Need eligibility rules so we don't overload interns/new LMs.

ops-bot: Eligibility: >6 months tenure, <18 pending, not on LOA, not in current calibration panel. Weekly cap default 30 handbacks.

Sasha: Can managers opt their team members out quickly? Some folks are heads-down.

Maya: Yes  managers can set a quick opt-out toggle in console Teams > Review Settings. Opt-out lasts 48h by default.

Priya: What about reviewers currently at 26 pending? System tends to ping them during surge. We should avoid pushing them over 30.

ops-bot: Surge guardrail: do not assign to reviewers who would exceed 30 pending. If no volunteers meet criteria, system suggests short-term reassignment to a cross-team pool and notifies leads for manual approval.

Owen: Operationally, can we open a temporary "surge channel" for volunteers and leads to coordinate?

Maya: Creating #people-ops-surge now. I'll post a pinned message with quick checklists: how to opt-in, how to request reassign, and deep links to the roster CSV.

Sasha: For audit, how do we mark items reassigned during surge so calibration reviewers understand context later?

Maya: Reassignments during surge will be tagged `surge_reassign:true` and include manager note + original reviewer in the audit log. We retain these for 3 years.

Priya: If a manager requests an exception (include post-freeze item in calibration), what's the rapid workflow during surge? People Ops might be swamped.

ops-bot: Exception fast-path: managers can request "expedite" with a mandatory 1-line justification. Ops will triage expedited exceptions within 12h during surge windows. Non-expedited follow standard 48h triage.

Owen: Sounds good. One last thing  can we surface a live counter in the console showing volunteer capacity vs projected surge so managers can see when to reassign earlier?

Maya: Adding a "Surge Capacity" widget to Console > Dashboards > Performance Ops. Will roll out in the next 4 hours. Meanwhile check `#people-ops-surge` pinned forecast.

ops-bot: Note: surge policy applied for final close day this cycle only. To extend, file a request at https://redwoodinference.internal/peopleops/surge.
